- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:step 5 (new content) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The sentence "A conflict only outside `.claude/` is never aborted so that the work can go on" is syntactically ambiguous.
  WHY: It is unclear if it means "is never (aborted so that the work can go on)" (intended) or "(is never aborted) (so that the work can go on)". A fixer reading this rule out of context could misinterpret the clause as allowing the sync merge to be aborted, reverting to the unsafe fail-open behavior identified in issue #5258. The twin file `.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md` uses the clearer phrasing "is resolved inside the sync merge, never aborted to continue on the unsynced head"; this file should be updated to match for consistency.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:step 5 (new content) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The cross-reference "On the project branch, step 2 resolves it as before." is ambiguous and potentially brittle.
  WHY: "Step 2" in the current Claude-asset sync subsection refers to the staleness-check step (`git diff --quiet ...`), not the merge or conflict resolution step. A future re-ordering or editing of the steps in this subsection could silently break this cross-reference, leading to incorrect behavior on project branches.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and its `.claude/commands/` twin):step 5 sentence "A conflict only outside `.claude/` is never aborted so that the work can go on: …" | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The phrase "is never aborted so that the work can go on" is grammatically awkward and parses ambiguously in English.
  WHY: A reader can read it as "the sync merge is sometimes aborted so the work can go on" (the opposite of the intent) before the colon explanation lands; the rest of the step (the colon clause, "On a PR head, resolve it inside the sync merge.", "Never continue the fix on the unsynced head.") only clarifies the intent after the confusing lead clause. The sibling rule in `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md` step 5 uses the unambiguous "is resolved inside the sync merge, never aborted to continue on the unsynced head". The two are the same shared rule (AD-2) and should mirror each other so a fixer session reading either twin in isolation reaches the same conclusion.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and its `.claude/commands/` twin):step 5 sentence "On the project branch, step 2 resolves it as before." | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Inside the `### Claude-asset sync` subsection, step 2 is the staleness-check (`git diff --quiet HEAD...origin/<default> -- .claude/hooks .claude/settings.json`), not the merge or conflict step.
  WHY: The text intends to reference the implement-plan flow's step 2 (the session-start sync that drives the Claude-asset sync on the project branch) but the bare "step 2" inside this subsection points at the local step 2 by default. The original #4952 text had the same ambiguity and the new wording preserves it; "as before" assumes the reader already knows which step 2 is meant. A future edit that renumbers the Claude-asset sync's own steps (e.g. adds a new leading step before `Stale?`) silently invalidates the cross-reference without breaking any contract test. A reader who follows the literal "step 2" lands on a `git diff --quiet` command that has nothing to do with conflict resolution and may incorrectly conclude that the staleness check itself resolves the conflict.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:Claude-asset sync step 5, sentence "A conflict only outside `.claude/` is never aborted so that the work can go on" | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The clause is syntactically ambiguous.
  WHY: A reader can parse it as "is never [aborted so that the work can go on]" (intended: the conflict is not aborted in order to continue on the unsynced head) or as "[is never aborted] [so that the work can go on]" (which says nothing useful). The twin in fix-claude-pr.md avoids the same ambiguity with clearer wording: "is resolved inside the sync merge, never aborted to continue on the unsynced head". A fixer session reading the implement-plan-claude.md rule out of context could misparse the clause and revert to the #4952 fail-open behavior (aborting the sync merge and continuing on the unsynced head), which is the exact security gap issue #5258 closes.
